title: Sir Ralph Boswell to his cousin William Boswell, Dec 1627 / Jan 1628, TNA SP 106/5 (DECODE R413; catalogued as King Charles I to Boswell)

steps.what: Fetched DECODE R413 with the shared cookie: two page images and two PDFs, a 'cryptanalysis' and a 'key'.
The cryptanalysis PDF is Mark Woodard's 2021 decipherment (CrypTool 2 monoalphabetic analyzer): an English newsletter on Buckingham's return from Plymouth, three signs left as '?'.
Aligned Woodard's 442-letter transcription with his plaintext: each of 21 transcription letters maps to one plaintext letter without exception (l = B once reads O, a slip for R in LOLDES).
Resolved his gaps from context: p = S (HI[S] OWNE; OUR[S]), second w = a code or abbreviation for 'part' (FOR THE MOST [PART] ARE). The pair w x after 'conceaued he' stays unread.

Read the endorsement on p. 2 as 'Sr Ra: Boswele. 24 Jan. 1627': the sender is Sir Ralph Boswell, a kinsman ('my ... Cosin'), not Charles I. Saturday the 15th falls (Julian) in Dec 1627 or Mar 1628; with receipt on 24 Jan 1627/8 the letter's day is 15 Dec 1627.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): transcription.txt (Woodard's transcription); the reading copied verbatim from NOTES.md to texts/R413_decryption.md, with Woodard's own decipherment linked on DECODE R413; the key copied from NOTES.md to texts/key.md.

outcome.method_basis: Mark Woodard's 2021 key and transcription on DECODE R413 were on the record before the attempt; the project filled the signs he left open.
outcome.notes: Solved by Woodard 2021. Added here: the gap readings, the sender (Sir Ralph Boswell, not the King) and the date from the endorsement. Catalogue entry 63 removed.

credits.note: monoalphabetic key, transcription and plaintext on DECODE R413; open signs filled here

texts.label: Sir Ralph Boswell to William Boswell, c. 15 Dec 1627
texts.summary: Sir Ralph Boswell tells his kinsman William Boswell that Buckingham ('our greate Duke') has returned from Plymouth to Whitehall after the failed Île de Ré expedition, sure of the King's favour against his enemies in the Commons and backed in the Lords by the bishops and the new peers of his own making. texts/R413_decryption.md is the project's text (Woodard's key plus the gap readings of 2026); Mark Woodard's 2021 transcription and plaintext are on the DECODE record (PDF DOC_413_2021-Nov-09).

human: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
